candidates.name: Entropy
candidates.definition: Predicting and explaining the sign of ΔS from dispersal of matter and energy (phase, moles of gas, volume, temperature), and calculating ΔS° from standard molar entropies.
candidates.include: Tag when the sign or value of an entropy change must be predicted, explained or calculated, or substances ranked by entropy.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag ΔG sign analysis unless the entropy sign must be determined as part of it (then entropy is supporting).

candidates.name: Energy of phase changes
candidates.definition: Heat absorbed or released during melting, vaporization, freezing and condensation (q = nΔH), constant temperature during a phase change, and heating or cooling curves.
candidates.include: Tag when enthalpies of fusion or vaporization, heating curves, or phase-change energy must be used.

candidates.name: Thermodynamics of dissolution
candidates.definition: Explaining whether a salt dissolves through the balance of lattice and hydration interactions (ΔH) and the entropy change (ΔS) of dissolving.
candidates.include: Tag when the enthalpy, entropy or free energy of dissolution must be explained or predicted.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag Ksp calculations (tag solubility-product).

candidates.name: Intermolecular forces and physical properties
candidates.definition: Using the relative strength of intermolecular forces to explain or rank boiling point, melting point, vapor pressure, viscosity, surface tension or enthalpy of vaporization, and distinguishing intermolecular from intramolecular forces.
candidates.include: Tag when a physical property must be compared or explained in terms of intermolecular attractions; pair with the specific force concept(s) that decide the comparison.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag chemical reactivity or bond-breaking explanations; boiling does not break covalent bonds.

candidates.name: Particle model of solids, liquids and gases
candidates.definition: Describing the arrangement, spacing and motion of particles in solids, liquids and gases, and recognizing phase changes as physical changes.
candidates.include: Tag when particle arrangement or motion across phases must be described, drawn or interpreted.
candidates.exclude: Phase diagrams are not assessed; do not tag energy calculations for phase changes (tag phase-change-energy).

candidates.name: Hydrogen bonding
candidates.definition: The strong dipole attraction between an H atom bonded to N, O or F and a lone pair on a nearby N, O or F atom.
candidates.include: Tag when hydrogen bonding must be identified, drawn, or used to explain a property, including identifying donors and acceptors.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag molecules that contain H and O but no H bonded to N, O or F (a common error).

candidates.name: Moles, molar mass and particle counts
candidates.definition: Converting among mass, moles and number of particles using molar mass and Avogadro's number, including counting atoms within a formula.
candidates.include: Tag when the student must perform or reason about a mass-mole-particle conversion that is a substantive step, or the question is about the mole itself.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when a mole conversion is an unremarkable first step of a larger stoichiometry, gas or solution calculation already captured by another concept, unless the question isolates it.

candidates.name: Calorimetry and specific heat
candidates.definition: Using q = mcΔT, heat capacity and calorimeter data to determine heat transferred or the enthalpy change of a process, and evaluating calorimetry procedures and errors.
candidates.include: Tag when calorimetry data or q = mcΔT must be used, or a calorimetry procedure or error analyzed.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag phase-change heat (q = nΔH) alone (tag phase-change-energy).

candidates.name: Gibbs free energy and favorability
candidates.definition: Using ΔG° = ΔH° - TΔS° and the signs of ΔH and ΔS to determine thermodynamic favorability and the temperature at which favorability changes.
candidates.include: Tag when ΔG must be calculated or its sign reasoned from ΔH and ΔS, or a crossover temperature found.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag ΔG-K or ΔG-E relationships alone (tag free-energy-equilibrium or cell-potential).
